texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.Why are you interested in Runpod?:
Runpod is where my two halves meet.

The operator half: for the last three years I have run AI in production rather than talked about it - a six-machine Claude fleet operated in public, with MCP connectors, RAG over a ten-year knowledge base, an AI-native CRM and 100+ unattended automation routines. More to the point for this role, I publish evals and a public FAILURE-MODES document instead of a demo reel; the July 2026 measurement (0 of 17 high-risk actions slipped past the human approval gate in recorded runs) is out in the open with the cases where it does break. I know exactly what a developer hits between 'the model works' and 'it runs every night', which is the gap an FDE team lives in.

The leadership half is older. I co-founded a software house and incubator in APAC in 2015 and ran a distributed engineering org of 40+ developers as product owner; up to 30 operators worked daily inside the CRM I wrote; I ran cohorts end to end and did enterprise advisory for subsidiaries of Foxconn and ANA Airlines. Building structure where little exists - playbooks, triage frameworks, onboarding, knowledge-base architecture - is the part I actually enjoy. After 10,000+ founder calls and 2,000+ institutional-investor calls I am equally comfortable in an architecture discussion and in front of an unhappy enterprise sponsor.

What draws me specifically: a million developers and 20 [человек] inference requests is the scale where field signal is a genuine product input, and a function that owns both FDE and Tier 1-3 support is where that signal becomes a roadmap instead of a ticket backlog. I would rather build that conduit than manage around it.
